item.title: Puget Sound marine areas 8-2 and 9 salmon fishing update
item.description:
Action: Reduces the salmon daily limit to one effective Monday, Sept. 21.

Species affected: Salmon.

Location and effective dates:

  • Marine Area 8-2 (Port Susan and Port Gardner), except the Tulalip Terminal Area:
    • Sept. 21–25, 2026.
  • Marine Area 9 (Admiralty Inlet):
    • Sept. 21–30, 2026.

Salmon rules: No minimum size. Daily limit one. Release Chinook and chum.

Reason for action: Recreational coho catches have far exceeded pre-season expectations in marine areas 8-2 and 9 this year. Extreme terminal and freshwater areas of 8-2 have not seen signals of high abundance, and freshwater environmental conditions including low water could be affecting migratory behavior of returning coho. A reduction to the daily limit in catch areas 8-2 and 9 is a precautionary measure to ensure that conservation objectives for coho in the Stillaguamish and Snohomish rivers are met.

Additional information: Fishery managers encourage anglers to sign up for Fishing Rule Change email notifications and to check for emergency rules on the WDFW website before fishing. Refer to the Washington Sport Fishing Rules pamphlet for current regulations. Download the Fish Washington® mobile app to stay up to date on the go.

item.title: Lake Washington reopens for salmon fishing
item.description:
Action: Returns Lake Washington to permanent rules listed in the Washington Sport Fishing Rules, reopening salmon fishing.

Effective dates: Immediately through Oct. 31, 2026.

Species affected: Coho salmon.

Location: Lake Washington (King County) north of Highway 520 Bridge and east of Montlake Bridge, including the portion of the Sammamish River near Kenmore from 68th Avenue Northeast downstream.

Reason for action: Fish counts at the Ballard Locks have improved significantly over the past week, indicating the coho return to the Lake Washington/Lake Sammamish basin is sufficient to reopen coho retention in Lake Washington.

Additional information: Preliminary salmon counts collected during survey hours at the Ballard Locks are available on WDFW’s Lake Washington salmon counts webpage.

item.title: North Fork Stillaguamish to close to all fishing and Stillaguamish River mainstem to remain closed until further notice
item.description:
Action: Closes recreational fishing in the North Fork Stillaguamish River and postpones the opening of the mainstem Stillaguamish River.

Species affected: All species.

Effective dates: Sept. 18, 2026, until further notice.

Locations:

  • North Fork Stillaguamish River, from the mouth to the Highway 530 bridge (Cicero Bridge) near Oso.
  • Stillaguamish River, from Marine Drive to the confluence of the North and South forks.

Rules: Closed to fishing.

Reason for action: Low water flows have resulted in Chinook salmon holding in the lower river and not moving upstream to spawning grounds, resulting in greater than expected Chinook encounter rates. This temporary closure will reduce impacts on Stillaguamish Chinook populations until flows increase and allow Chinook to leave the lower river. Limited allowable take of Chinook in the Stillaguamish system necessitates this action to preserve coho opportunity later in the fall.

Additional information: Fishery managers plan to reopen recreational fisheries when the majority of Chinook are no longer present in the system. More information on Stillaguamish Chinook recovery and habitat restoration efforts is available on this WDFW webpage.

item.title: Tucannon River hatchery steelhead fishing update
item.description:
Action: Reduces hatchery steelhead daily limit.

Species affected: Hatchery steelhead.

Location: Tucannon River from the mouth to the Tucannon Hatchery Road bridge.

Effective dates: Sept. 18, 2026, until further notice.

Rules:

  • Open daily.
    • Daily limit 1 hatchery steelhead.
    • Barbless hooks required.

Reason for action: The total A/B-index and unclipped steelhead returns at Bonneville Dam are currently the lowest on record since the dam was constructed in 1938.

On Sept. 14, the U.S. v. Oregon Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) downgraded the expected total steelhead return at Bonneville Dam to 61,500 fish, which would be the lowest total return on record. The total includes 53,400 A-index steelhead, of which 17,500 are unclipped, and 8,100 B-index steelhead, of which 2,900 are unclipped.

While the overall return is low, current return estimates for natural- and hatchery-origin steelhead are high enough to allow for some recreational fisheries to continue with reduced daily limits.

Additional information:

  • WDFW requires that all Washington licensed anglers cease fishing for steelhead once they have retained their daily limit.
  • Two-pole fishing is now allowed during this fishery.
  • Anglers should be sure to identify their catch, as coho and Chinook salmon are also present in the Tucannon River during this fishery.
  • All salmonids (salmon or steelhead) that are not kept as part of the daily limit cannot be removed from the water and must be immediately released unharmed. All fall Chinook adults and jacks must be immediately released unharmed. All Chinook adults and jacks must be immediately recorded upon retention, no a catch record card, when utilizing a Washington fishing license.
  • All anglers age 15 and older must possess a Columbia River salmon and steelhead endorsement (CRSSE) to fish recreationally for salmon and steelhead in the Columbia River and many of its Washington tributaries. The CRSSE is an annual requirement in addition to a valid fishing license. Endorsements are available to purchase online.

Fishery managers encourage anglers to sign up for Fishing Rule Change email notifications and to check for emergency rules on the WDFW website before fishing. Refer to the Washington Sport Fishing Rules pamphlet for current regulations. Download the Fish Washington® mobile app to stay up to date on the go.

item.title: Snake River hatchery steelhead fishing update
item.description:
Action: Reduces hatchery steelhead daily limits.

Species affected: Hatchery steelhead.

Effective dates: Sept. 18, 2026, until further notice.

Location and rules:

From the mouth of the Snake River (Burbank to Pasco railroad bridge at Snake River mile 1.25) to the Lower Granite dam (Catch Record Card (CRC) areas 640, 642, 644 and 646):

  • Open daily.
  • Daily limit one hatchery steelhead.
  • Barbless hooks required.

From Lower Granite Dam upstream to the Oregon state line (CRC areas 648 and 650):

  • Open daily.
    • Daily limit two hatchery steelhead.
    • Barbless hooks required.

Reason for action: The total A/B index and unclipped steelhead returns at Bonneville Dam are currently the lowest on record since the dam was constructed in 1938.

On Sept. 14, the U.S. v. Oregon Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) downgraded the total expected steelhead return at Bonneville Dam to 61,500 fish, which would be the lowest total return on record. The total includes 53,400 A-index steelhead, of which 17,500 are unclipped, and 8,100 total B-index steelhead, of which 2,900 are unclipped.

WDFW has coordinated with comanagers, and while the overall return is low, current return estimates for natural- and hatchery-origin steelhead returning to the Snake River are high enough to allow for some recreational fisheries to continue with reduced daily limits.

Additional information: 

  • WDFW requires that all Washington licensed anglers cease fishing for steelhead once they have retained their daily limit.
  • Two-pole fishing is not allowed during this fishery.
  • When fishing in the Snake River between Washington and Idaho, the holder of a valid Washington fishing license may fish the Snake River where it forms a boundary between the states of Washington and Idaho. Washington licensed anglers are subject to the Washington fishing rules and may not fish from the Idaho shore, including wading, and may not fish sloughs or tributaries on the Idaho side.
  • Any angler who fishes on the Snake River or any other water forming a Washington boundary can only utilize the fishing privileges (limits, size restriction, etc.) of one state’s fishing license at a time. Before utilizing a Washington fishing license or fishing Washington-only waters, any fish retained while using another state’s license must be returned to shore before continuing to angle.
  • Areas listed as Closed Waters in the Washington Sport Fishing Rules pamphlet, remain closed.
  • Anglers should be sure to identify their catch, as coho and Chinook salmon are also present in the Snake River during this fishery.
  • All salmonids (salmon or steelhead) that are not kept as part of the daily limit cannot be removed from the water and must be immediately released unharmed. All fall Chinook adults and jacks must be immediately recorded upon retention, on a catch record card when utilizing a Washington fishing license.
  • All anglers age 15 and older must possess a Columbia River salmon and steelhead endorsement (CRSSE) to fish recreationally for salmon and steelhead in the Columbia River and many of its Washington tributaries. The CRSSE is an annual requirement in addition to a valid fishing license. Endorsements are available to purchase online.

Fishery managers encourage anglers to sign up for Fishing Rule Change email notifications and to check for emergency rules on the WDFW website before fishing. Refer to the Washington Sport Fishing Rules pamphlet for current regulations. Download the Fish Washington® mobile app to stay up to date on the go.

item.title: Snake River fall Chinook fishery update
item.description:
Action: Closes retention of wild (unmarked) adult Chinook in Snake River beginning Sept. 18.

Species affected: Chinook salmon.

Location, dates, and rules:

Lyons Ferry Bubble Fishery: From the red river marker (Marker 28) on the south shore of the Snake River upstream to the Highway 261 bridge (approximately 1.4 miles):

  • Sept. 16:
    • Closed.
  • Sept. 17:
    • Daily limit two adult Chinook, including no more than one wild adult Chinook. No daily limit for jack Chinook (wild or hatchery). Minimum size 12 inches. Release all salmon other than Chinook.
  • Sept. 18–Oct. 25, 2026:
    • Open Thursday through Sunday each week:
    • Daily limit two adult hatchery Chinook. No daily limit for jack Chinook (wild or hatchery). Minimum size 12 inches. Release all salmon other than jack Chinook and adult hatchery Chinook.
    • Barbless hooks required.

From the downstream edge of the large power lines crossing the Snake River just upstream of West Evans Road on the south shore (approximately three miles downstream of Clarkston), upstream to the Washington/Idaho state line (top of Catch Record Card area 648):

  • Sept. 16–Sept. 17:
    • Open daily.
    • Daily limit three adult Chinook, including no more than one wild adult Chinook. No daily limit for jack Chinook (wild or hatchery). Minimum size 12 inches. Release all salmon other than Chinook.
    • Barbless hooks required.
  • Sept. 18–Oct. 15, 2026:
    • Open daily.
    • Daily limit three adult hatchery Chinook. No limit for jack Chinook (wild or hatchery). Minimum size 12 inches. Release all salmon other than jack Chinook and adult hatchery Chinook.
    • Barbless hooks required.

From the Washington/Idaho state line to the Oregon state line (Catch Record Card area 650):

  • Sept. 16–Sept. 17:
    • Open daily.
    • Daily limit three adult Chinook, including no more than one wild adult Chinook. No daily limit for jack Chinook (wild or hatchery). Minimum size 12 inches. Release all salmon other than Chinook.
    • Barbless hooks required.
  • Sept. 18–Oct. 31, 2026:
    • Open daily.
    • Daily limit three adult hatchery Chinook. No limit for jack Chinook (wild or hatchery). Minimum size 12 inches. Release all salmon other than jack Chinook and adult hatchery Chinook.
    • Barbless hooks required.

Reason for action: WDFW met with comanagers to review the in-season harvest of unmarked fall Chinook salmon and associated impacts to natural-origin fish from recreational fisheries. Based on current harvest levels, it is necessary to shift to a mark-selective fishery for adult Chinook to extend opportunity to harvest hatchery fish while minimizing impacts on natural-origin fish.

Additional information:

  • WDFW requires that all Washington licensed anglers cease fishing for Chinook once they have retained their adult daily limit. Adult Chinook are 24 inches in length or larger and jack Chinook are less than 24 inches in length.
  • Two-pole fishing is not allowed during this fishery.
  • When fishing in the Snake River between Washington and Idaho, the holder of a valid Washington fishing license may fish the Snake River where it forms a boundary between the states of Washington and Idaho. Washington licensed anglers are subject to the Washington fishing rules and may not fish from the Idaho shore, including wading, and may not fish sloughs or tributaries on the Idaho side.
  • Any angler who fishes on the Snake River or any other water forming a Washington boundary can only utilize the fishing privileges (limits, size restriction, etc.) of one state’s fishing license at a time. Before utilizing a Washington fishing license or fishing Washington only waters, any fish retained while using another state’s license must be returned to shore before continuing to angle.
  • Areas listed as Closed Waters in the Washington Sport Fishing Rules pamphlet, remain closed.
  • Anglers should be sure to identify their catch, as coho salmon and steelhead are also present in the Snake River during this fishery.
  • All salmonids (salmon or steelhead) that are not kept as part of the daily limit cannot be removed from the water and must be immediately released unharmed. All fall Chinook adults and jacks must be immediately recorded upon retention, on a catch record card when utilizing a Washington fishing license.
  • All anglers age 15 and older must possess a Columbia River salmon and steelhead endorsement (CRSSE) to fish recreationally for salmon and steelhead in the Columbia River and many of its Washington tributaries. The CRSSE is an annual requirement in addition to a valid fishing license. Endorsements are available to purchase online.

item.title: Satsop River temporarily closes to fishing through Sept. 30
item.description:
Action: Temporary closure on the Satsop River.

Effective date:  Sept. 16–30, 2026.

Species affected: Game fish.

Locations: Satsop River (Grays Harbor County) from the mouth to the Bingham Creek Hatchery dam.

Rules: Closed to fishing.

Reason for action: Disorderly fishing behavior has been observed on the Satsop River during enforcement patrols, with anglers observed targeting salmon before the planned the Oct. 1 salmon season opener. Low river flows in the basin are also affecting salmon migration, making fish more vulnerable than normal to angling activity.

While pre-season planning accounted for some incidental mortality of Chinook during the September gamefish season, it did not account for the levels of incidental mortality experienced when anglers are targeting salmon or current low river flows. Because of these conditions, natural origin Chinook require additional conservation measures.

The closure is intended to prevent further impacts to Chinook in September while preserving impacts for the coho-directed fishery scheduled to begin in October.

Additional Information: This closure includes the section from 400 feet below Bingham Creek Hatchery dam to the dam Catch Record Code (CRC) 329A. 

Fishery managers encourage anglers to sign up for Fishing Rule Change email notifications and to check for emergency rules on the WDFW website before fishing. Refer to the Washington Sport Fishing Rules pamphlet for current regulations. Download the Fish Washington® mobile app to stay up to date on the go.

item.title: Skagit and Cascade River fishing updates
item.description:
Action: Postpones opening of fishing seasons in upper areas of the Skagit River and Cascade River and temporarily closes all fishing in the Skagit River from Gilligan Creek east of Sedro-Wolley to the Dalles Bridge near Concrete. This rule also reduces the salmon daily limit, prohibits bait, and requires single-point barbless hooks in the Skagit River from the mouth to Gilligan Creek.

Effective date: Sept. 14, 2026, until further notice.

Species affected: All species, coho salmon.

Specific locations and rules:

Skagit River from the mouth to Gilligan Creek:

  • Salmon: Minimum size 12 inches. Daily limit two coho. Release all salmon other than coho. Bait prohibited and single-point barbless hooks required.

Skagit River from Gilligan Creek to Marblemount Bridge:

  • Closed to fishing for all species.

Cascade River from mouth to Rockport-Cascade Rd. Bridge:

  • Closed to fishing for all species.

Reason for action: With the combination of low river flows and greater than average Chinook encounter rates during the coho fishery in the lower Skagit River that opened on Aug. 16, including misidentified Chinook being retained, this action is necessary to preserve coho opportunity in October when the majority of the largest forecasted wild coho return in decades is expected to be in the river.

Preseason regulations were designed around efforts to increase opportunity and harvest of hatchery coho within Chinook encounter guidelines that have been sufficient in the past. As of Sept. 11 nearly half of the available Chinook impacts have been used weeks ahead of the normal mid-point of the coho fishery. This rule will shift focus from catching more hatchery coho to preserving opportunity for retaining wild coho later in the season. These measures will preserve harvest opportunity over 29 miles of river with a non-selective daily limit of two coho, wild or hatchery.

Additional information on sport fisheries: Dolly Varden/bull trout are closed, and a night closure is in effect in Skagit River from the mouth to Gilligan Creek.

item.title: Yakima River fall salmon fishery to open
item.description:
Action: Opens the lower Yakima River salmon retention.

Effective date: Sept. 15-Oct. 31, 2026.

Species affected: Chinook and coho salmon.

Location: Yakima River from the Highway 240 bridge in Richland (river mile 2.1) to the Grant Avenue Bridge in Prosser (river mile 47.0). 

Rules: Minimum size 12 inches. Daily limit of one adult. No limit on jacks. Release all salmon other than Chinook and coho. Night closure in effect. Barbless hooks are required. 

Reason for action: Current fish passage through the Prosser Diversion Dam indicates the fall Chinook return is sufficient to provide sport fishing opportunity for anglers in the lower Yakima River.

Additional information: Anglers must stop fishing for salmon once they have retained their adult daily limit.  Fishing remains closed from 200 feet downstream of the United States Bureau of Reclamation (USBR) Chandler Powerhouse/Spillway to 200 feet upstream of the USBR Chandler Powerhouse.

A Columbia River Salmon and Steelhead Endorsement is required for all anglers age 15 and older fishing for salmon or steelhead on the Columbia River or its tributaries (including Yakima River).

Fishery managers will continue to monitor the return and announce any additional changes to the fishery if necessary.

Fishery managers encourage anglers to sign up for Fishing Rule Change email notifications and to check for emergency rules on the WDFW website before fishing. Refer to the Washington Sport Fishing Rules for current regulation. Download the Fish Washington® mobile app to stay up to date on the go.

item.title: Lower Columbia River salmon and steelhead fishery update
item.description:
Action: Allows retention of one additional adult hatchery coho as part of the daily limit from the Buoy 10 line upstream to the west end of Puget Island.

Species affected: Salmon.

Effective date: Sept. 12–Oct. 31, 2026.

Locations and rules:

From a north-south line through Buoy 10 to the Rocky Point/Tongue Point line (a projected line from Rocky Point on the Washington bank through Red Buoy 44, to the red navigation marker 2 at Tongue Point on the Oregon bank):

  • Sept. 12–30: Salmon and steelhead daily limit three salmon. Coho minimum size 16 inches. Release all salmon and steelhead other than hatchery coho.
  • Oct. 1–31: Salmon and steelhead daily limit six, including up to three adults. Salmon minimum size 12 inches. Release all salmon and steelhead other than hatchery coho.

From the Rocky Point/Tongue Point line upstream to a line at the west end of Puget Island, projected from green navigation marker 39 on the Washington bank to green navigation marker 41, then to red navigation marker 42, and terminating at red navigation marker 44A on the Oregon bank:

  • Sept. 12–Oct 31: Salmon and steelhead daily limit six, including up to three adults. Salmon minimum size 12 inches. Release all salmon and steelhead other than hatchery coho.

Reason for action: The Buoy 10 coho fishery is tracking below expectations for unclipped coho mortalities as compared to the preseason fishing plan. Sufficient Endangered Species Act (ESA) impacts are available to provide additional hatchery coho harvest opportunity.

Additional information: Anglers are reminded that continuing to fish for jack salmon is prohibited once the daily adult salmon limit has been retained.

item.title: Quillayute River closing to all fishing due to low flows and poor water conditions
item.description:
Action: Closes fishing.

Effective dates: Sept. 9, 2026, until further notice.

Species affected: All species.

Location: Quillayute River (Clallam County) from the Olympic National Park boundary upstream to the confluence of Sol Duc and Bogachiel rivers.

Rules: Closed to all fishing.

Reason for action: Recent rains to the Olympic Peninsula have not been substantial enough to mitigate for ongoing low flows and poor river conditions in the Quillayute River. Low flows have resulted in Chinook and coho holding in the lower river and not moving upstream to the spawning grounds, resulting in increased fishing pressure while the fish are more susceptible to harvest and handling mortalities. Returning salmon abundance will be monitored and regulations may be modified as additional information becomes available.

Additional information: Fishery managers encourage anglers to sign up for Fishing Rule Change email notifications and to check for emergency rules on the WDFW website before fishing. item.title: Marine Area 9 (Admiralty Inlet), Marine Area 12 (Hood Canal) shellfish beaches update
item.description:
Action: Rescinds biotoxin-related closure of public shellfish beaches in Dabob and Quilcene bays and at Belfair State Park; and opens oyster harvest at Point Whitney Tidelands and Lagoon. Maintains other previously announced shellfish beach closures in marine areas 9 (Admiralty Inlet) and 12 (Hood Canal).

Effective dates: Sept. 3, 2026, until further notice.

Species affected: Clams, mussels, and oysters.

Locations and rules:

  • Marine Area 9:
    • All public beaches south of a line drawn from Foulweather Bluff to Olele Point: Closed to harvest.
  • Marine Area 12:
    • All public beaches, except those with current harvest seasons in Dabob and Quilcene bays north of a line drawn eastward from the southern boundary of Seal Rock U.S. Forest Service Campground to Zelatched Point, and Belfair State Park: Closed to harvest.
    • Public beaches in Dabob and Quilcene bays north of a line drawn eastward from the southern boundary of Seal Rock U.S. Forest Service Campground to Zelatched Point, and Belfair State Park: Follow seasons listed on WDFW Clam, mussel, and oyster harvest public beach webpages, searchable using the WDFW Find a Beach tool or the Washington Shellfish Safety Map.
    • Point Whitney Tidelands and Lagoon: Open to oyster harvest through Sept. 30.

Reason for action: Clam, mussel, and oyster conditions and biotoxin status previously determined by the Washington State Department of Health (DOH) to be unsafe have subsided in Dabob and Quilcene bays for some species, and in portions of southern Hood Canal, allowing for a lifting of the closure to recreational shellfish harvest from public beaches in these areas. The DOH closure remains in place for butter and varnish clams in Dabob and Quilcene Bays while other species such as Manila clams and Pacific oysters are safe. Belfair State Park is safe and open for all species.

Additional information: DOH advises against harvest and consumption of butter clams and varnish clams in areas that are open to shellfish harvest in Dabob and Quilcene bays. A bivalve shellfish identification guide (PDF) is available online from DOH and WDFW.

This action maintains the previous WDFW closure of a portion of Marine Area 9, but harvesters should be aware of DOH status in other parts of Marine Area 9 before harvesting.

Oyster seasons have been extended at the Point Whitney Tidelands and Lagoon through Sept. 30 to offset lost opportunity there; these beaches remain closed to clam harvest to allow recovery of clam populations. Other Hood Canal beaches may see season extensions when biotoxin status allows for reopening.

Always check the Washington Shellfish Safety Map before harvesting and the WDFW beach page for the beach you are visiting to confirm seasons are open.

item.title: Marine Area 1 (Ilwaco) recreational salmon season update
item.description:
Action: Opens five days of hatchery coho retention (Sept. 4–8) with a nearshore salmon fishing closure.

Species affected: Salmon.

Locations, dates, and rules:

Marine Area 1, outside of the nearshore salmon closure area:

  • Sept. 1–3: Closed to salmon fishing. Possession of salmon is prohibited onboard a vessel.
  • Sept. 4–8: Daily limit two. Coho minimum size 16 inches. Other salmon species no minimum size. Release Chinook and wild coho. Possession of Chinook is prohibited onboard a vessel.
  • Sept. 9–30: Closed to salmon fishing. Possession of salmon is prohibited onboard a vessel.

Marine Area 1 nearshore salmon closure area, north of 46° 15’ N and east of 124° 08.667’ W (from approximately mid-mouth Columbia River north and within approximately 3 miles of shore):

  • Sept. 1–3: Closed to salmon fishing. Possession of salmon is prohibited onboard a vessel.
  • Sept. 4–8: Closed to salmon fishing. Possession of Chinook is prohibited onboard a vessel.
  • Sept. 9–30: Closed to salmon fishing. Possession of salmon is prohibited onboard a vessel.

Reason for action: Current catch estimates indicate sufficient coho remain under the quota to allow for this limited opening.

Additional information: The Columbia River Control Zone is closed to salmon fishing, except open to fishing from the north jetty when adjacent waters north of the Control Zone (Marine Area 1) or the Buoy 10 fishery (Columbia River from Buoy 10 to the Astoria-Megler Bridge) are open to fishing for salmon. Salmon minimum size and daily limits in the north jetty follow the most liberal regulations from either Marine Area 1 or the Buoy 10 fishery.

item.title: Daily limits removed from Fish Lake ahead of rehabilitation
item.description:
Action: Opens fishing with no size restrictions or daily limit for all species.

Species affected: All species

Location: Fish Lake (Spokane County)

Effective dates: Immediately through Oct. 17, 2026.

Rules:

  • Open for fishing with no size restriction or daily limit for all species.
  • Fishing from a vessel equipped with an internal combustion engine is prohibited.

Reason for action: Fish Lake is scheduled to be treated with rotenone, a naturally occurring piscide commonly used to remove undesirable and illegally stocked fish species from lakes and streams. For additional information, see WDFW’s Pre-treatment plan for Fish Lake (PDF).

Additional information: Fish Lake is closed beginning Oct. 18.

item.title: Stevens Creek to close to fishing in September
item.description:
Action: Closes game fish angling in Stevens Creek.

Effective date: Sept. 1–30, 2026.

Species affected: Game fish

Locations: Stevens Creek in Grays Harbor County from the mouth to the U.S. Highway 101 Bridge.

Rules: Closed to fishing.

Reason for actions: Humptulips Salmon Hatchery broodstock goals have not been met in three of the last four years, and the pre-season hatchery return forecast is less than half of the recent average. Chinook stage in Stevens Creek before entering the hatchery. Current low flows are hindering their ability to access the hatchery intake, leaving them vulnerable to fishing pressure. This closure is necessary to improve chances of meeting hatchery broodstock goals by reducing impacts on Chinook staging to enter the hatchery.

Additional information: Fishing in this section is closed October through November, as listed in the 2026–2027 Washington Sport Fishing Rules pamphlet.

item.description:

item.title: Lower Naselle River gear restriction update
item.description:
Action: Rescinds requirement for bait or lure to be suspended below a float, except when trolling from a floating device, beginning Oct. 15.

Effective dates: Oct. 15–31, 2026

Species affected: All species.

Location: Naselle River, from the confluence of the South Fork upstream to the Highway 4 bridge.

Reason for action: The end date for this restriction was inadvertently changed during recent steelhead and trout rule making.

The suspended gear rule is intended to deter anglers from snagging early returning hatchery Chinook, as these fish are particularly vulnerable during low water in the early season. By late October, the hatchery run is dwindling and the water is higher, making snagging much less of an issue. Additionally, leaving the rule in place would hinder other fisheries, particularly coho.

item.description:
Action: Opens Puget Sound summer crab season in Marine Area 7 North Thursday through Monday each week, from Aug. 15–Sept. 28, 2026.

Species affected: Dungeness, Red Rock, and Tanner crab.

Updated Effective Dates and Locations: 

Marine areas 4 east of the Bonilla-Tatoosh line, 5, 6, 8-1, 8-2, and 9:

  • Open Thursday through Monday each week, from July 2–Sept. 7, 2026.

Sub-area 7 South (Those waters of Marine Area 7 south and west of a line projected from Village Point, Lummi Island, through the navigation buoy just east of Matia Island, thence to the buoy at Clements Reef, thence to the easternmost point of Patos Island, thence running along the northern shore of Patos Island to the westernmost point of Patos Island, thence true west to the international boundary and south of a line that extends from Point Francis on Portage Island, through the marker just north of Inati Bay on Lummi Island to Lummi Island):

  • Open Thursday through Monday each week, from July 16–Sept. 28, 2026.

Sub-area 7 North (Those waters of Marine Area 7 north and east of a line projected from Village Point, Lummi Island through the navigation buoy just east of Matia Island thence to the buoy at Clements Reef thence to the easternmost point of Patos Island, running along the northern shoreline of Patos Island and from the westernmost point of Patos Island true west to the international boundary and north of a line that extends from Point Francis on Portage Island, through the marker just north of Inati Bay on Lummi Island to Lummi Island):

  • Open Thursday through Monday each week, from Aug. 15–Sept. 28, 2026.

Marine Area 10:

  • Open Sunday and Monday each week, from July 5–Sept. 7, 2026.

Marine Area 11:

  • Open Sunday and Monday each week, from July 5–Aug. 17, 2026.

Marine Area 12 north of a line projected due east from Ayock Point:

  • Open Thursday through Monday each week, from July 2–Sept. 7, 2026.

Marine Area 12 south of a line projected due east from Ayock Point and Marine Area 13:

  • Closed until further notice.

Reason for action: State and Tribal co-managers have agreed that legal size Dungeness crabs have reached the hardshell criteria for harvest to schedule the opening for Marine Area 7 North. Crab seasons for the other marine areas remain as previously announced.

Additional information: The daily limits for crabs in all open Marine Areas will be 5 Dungeness, 6 Red Rock, and 6 Tanner.

When fishing from a vessel, gear may not be set or retrieved from one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise. Gear must be removed from the water on days closed to retention.

When fishing from land or land-based platforms (e.g. piers or docks) hand harvest and use of hand gear (dip nets, ring nets, shellfish pots, or any hand-operated, non-mechanized instrument) is open 24 hours per day on days open in that marine area.

All Dungeness crabs retained through Labor Day must be recorded immediately on a Summer Catch Record Card. Dungeness crabs retained after Labor Day must be recorded immediately on a Winter Catch Record Card.

item.title: Fall Chinook harvest to open in the Snake River
item.description:
Action: Opens Chinook salmon retention in areas of the Snake River.

Species affected: Chinook salmon.

Location, dates, and rules:

Lyons Ferry Bubble fishery: From the red river marker (Marker 28) on the south shore of the Snake River, upstream to the Highway 261 bridge (approximately 1.4 miles):

  • Sept. 3–Oct. 25, 2026
    • Open Thursday through Sunday each week.
    • Daily limit two adult Chinook, including no more than one wild adult Chinook. No daily limit for jack Chinook (wild or hatchery). Minimum size 12 inches. Release all salmon other than Chinook.
    • Barbless hooks required.

From the downstream edge of the large power lines crossing the Snake River just upstream of West Evans Road on the south shore (approximately three miles downstream of Clarkston), upstream to the Washington/Idaho state line (top of Catch Record Card area 648):

  • Aug. 18–Oct. 15, 2026
    • Open daily.
    • Daily limit three adult Chinook, including no more than one wild adult Chinook. No daily limit for jack Chinook (wild or hatchery). Minimum size 12 inches. Release all salmon other than Chinook.
    • Barbless hooks required.

From the Washington/Idaho state line to the Oregon state line (Catch Record Card area 650):

  • Aug. 18–Oct. 31, 2026
    • Open daily.
    • Daily limit three adult Chinook, including no more than one wild adult Chinook. No daily limit for jack Chinook (wild or hatchery). Minimum size 12 inches. Release all salmon other than Chinook.
    • Barbless hooks required.

Reason for action: The 2026 forecasted return of Columbia River upriver bright Chinook includes enough Snake River-origin fish to provide harvest opportunities. WDFW will monitor fall Chinook returns throughout the season and may close the fishery at any time due to harvest levels, ESA impacts, or in-season run adjustments.

Additional information:

  • WDFW requires that all Washington licensed anglers cease fishing for Chinook once they have retained their adult daily limit. Adult Chinook are 24 inches in length or larger and jack Chinook are less than 24 inches in length.
  • Two-pole fishing is not allowed during this fishery.
  • When fishing in the Snake River between Washington and Idaho, the holder of a valid Washington fishing license may fish the Snake River where it forms a boundary between the states of Washington and Idaho. Washington licensed anglers are subject to the Washington fishing rules and may not fish from the Idaho shore, including wading, and may not fish sloughs or tributaries on the Idaho side.
  • Any angler who fishes on the Snake River or any other water forming a Washington boundary can only utilize the fishing privileges (limits, size restriction, etc.) of one state’s fishing license at a time. Before utilizing a Washington fishing license or fishing Washington only waters, any fish retained while using another state’s license must be returned to shore before continuing to angle.
  • Anglers should be sure to identify their catch, as coho salmon and steelhead are also present in the Snake River during this fishery.
  • All salmonids (salmon or steelhead) that are not kept as part of the daily limit cannot be removed from the water and must be immediately released unharmed. All fall Chinook adults and jacks must be immediately recorded upon retention, on a catch record card when utilizing a Washington fishing license.
  • All anglers age 15 and older must possess a Columbia River salmon and steelhead endorsement (CRSSE) to fish recreationally for salmon and steelhead in the Columbia River and many of its Washington tributaries. The CRSSE is an annual requirement in addition to a valid fishing license. Endorsements are available to purchase online.

item.title: Summer halibut fishery 2026
item.description:
Action: Opens halibut dates in August and September. Annual halibut limit is six. Anglers may clean and portion halibut in the field but must retain the fish carcass until coming ashore.

Effective dates: August 8 – September 30, 2026 (See below for specific open days in each area.)

Species affected: Pacific halibut

Locations and specific open dates: 

Marine Area 1 (Ilwaco/Chinook):

  • The all-depth fishery is open August 8 – September 30 (seven days per week), as long as there is sufficient quota.
  • The fishery will be managed to 19,299 pounds.

Marine Area 2 (Westport):

  • The all-depth fishery is open August 8 – September 30 (seven days per week), as long as there is sufficient quota.
  • This area will be managed to an overall quota of 65,857 pounds.

Marine Areas 3 and 4 (Neah Bay and La Push):

  • Open August 16 – September 30 (seven days per week), as long as there is sufficient quota.
  • In Marine Area 4 east of the Bonilla-Tatoosh line, sablefish may be retained in waters seaward of the 120-foot bottomfish closure on days open for halibut.
  • The combined quota for both areas is 131,149 pounds.

Marine Area 5 (Sekiu) and Marine Areas 6 – 10 (Puget Sound):

  • Open August 16 – September 30 (seven days per week), as long as there is sufficient quota.
  • In waters seaward of the 120-foot bottomfish closure in Marine Area 5 sablefish may be retained on all days open for halibut
  • The total combined quota for all areas is 80,512 pounds.

Marine Areas 11–13 (Puget Sound):

  • Closed

Halibut Rules:

  • Daily limit 1 halibut, no minimum size. Annual limit 6 halibut. All catch must be immediately recorded on a WDFW catch record card.
  • Anglers may clean and portion halibut in the field but must retain the fish carcass until coming ashore.
  • Possession limit is two daily limits in any form, except only one daily limit while aboard the fishing vessel.

Reason for action: This emergency rule revises state rules, to conform with federal regulations. 

Additional information: Recreational halibut is quota managed, days open are dependent on available quota and areas will close when the quota is projected to be taken.

item.title: Puget Sound shrimp fishery update
item.description:
Updated Sept. 15 to correct the closing date for Marine Area 4 east of the Bonilla-Tatoosh line and Marine Area 5 to Sept. 16 as listed on Recreational shrimp fishing regulations by marine area webpage.

Action: Opens the fishery for all shrimp in Marine Area 6 except in the Discovery Bay Shrimp District on August 2. Opens the fishery for shrimp other than spot shrimp in Marine Area 6 except in the Discovery Bay Shrimp District from August 3 through October 15.

Species affected: All shrimp species which include spot shrimp, coonstripe shrimp, dock shrimp, pink shrimp, and sidestripe shrimp.

Updated effective dates by location: 

Marine Areas 4 east of the Bonilla-Tatoosh line and Marine Area 5:

  • Open through Sept. 15, 2026, for all shrimp species. Daylight hours only.

Marine Area 6 (excluding the Discovery Bay Shrimp District):

  • Open on Aug. 2, 2026, for all shrimp species, daylight hours only.
  • Open from Aug. 3 through Oct. 15, 2026, for shrimp species other than spot shrimp. It is unlawful to set or pull shrimp gear in waters greater than 175 feet deep. All spot shrimp caught must be immediately returned to the water unharmed.

Discovery Bay Shrimp District:

  • Closed.

Marine Area 7 East:

  • Open through Oct. 15, 2026, for shrimp species other than spot shrimp. It is unlawful to set or pull shrimp gear in waters greater than 200 feet deep. All spot shrimp caught must be immediately returned to the water unharmed.

Marine Area 7 South:

  • Closed.

Marine Area 7 West:

  • Closed.

Marine Areas 8-1 and 8-2:

  • Open through Oct. 15, 2026, for shrimp species other than spot shrimp. It is unlawful to set or pull shrimp gear in waters greater than 175 feet deep. All spot shrimp caught must be immediately returned to the water unharmed.

Marine Area 9:

  • Open through Oct. 15, 2026, for shrimp species other than spot shrimp. It is unlawful to set or pull shrimp gear in waters greater than 150 feet deep. All spot shrimp caught must be immediately returned to the water unharmed.

Marine Area 10:

  • The portion of Marine Area 10 east of a line from West Point to Alki Point (inside Elliott Bay) will remain closed.

Marine Area 10:

  • The portion of Marine Area 10 west of a line from West Point to Alki Point will remain closed.

Marine Area 11:

  • Open through Oct. 15, 2026, for shrimp species other than spot shrimp. It is unlawful to set or pull shrimp gear in waters greater than 150 feet deep. All spot shrimp caught must be immediately returned to the water unharmed.

Marine Area 12:

  • Closed.

Marine Area 13:

  • Open through Oct. 15, 2026, for shrimp species other than spot shrimp. It is unlawful to set or pull shrimp gear in waters greater than 200 feet deep. All spot shrimp caught must be immediately returned to the water unharmed.

Reason for action: Harvest and effort data from previous openings indicate the spot shrimp quotas for all areas except Marine Areas 4 (east of the Bonilla-Tatoosh line), 5, and 6 outside the Discovery Bay Shrimp District have been met. Opening Marine Area 6 outside the Discovery Bay Shrimp District on August 2 for all shrimp species, and non-spot shrimp species August 3 through October 15, this rule keeps the harvest of spot shrimp and non-spot shrimps consistent with State/Tribal management agreements.

Additional information: Find recreational shrimp fishing marine area information on the WDFW website. Information on shrimp identification, including non-spot shrimp, is also available on WDFW’s shrimp species webpages and identification guide (PDF) (PDF).

All-shrimp seasons, including spot shrimp: Pots with a minimum mesh size of one inch are allowed. The daily limit is 80 spot shrimp during the all-shrimp season, with a total daily weight limit of 10 pounds (whole shrimp), all species combined.

If retaining non-spot shrimp, all shrimp heads (spot and non-spot) must be retained in the field until ashore and finished fishing for the day. The daylight hours only rule indicates that pots can be set and retrieved from one hour before official sunrise to one hour after official sunset. All traps must be removed from the water during periods when fishing is closed.

Non-spot only seasons: Pots with a minimum mesh size of ½ inch are allowed. There are maximum fishing depth restrictions specific to each area to limit capture of spot shrimp. All spot shrimp must be immediately returned to the water unharmed. The daily limit is 10 pounds (whole shrimp), all species combined.

All shrimp heads must be retained in the field until ashore and finished fishing for the day. Pots can be set and retrieved from one hour before official sunrise to one hour after official sunset. All traps must be removed from the water during periods when fishing is closed.
